title: Dilly Dallying in Durango
summary:
We originally planned to spend two weekends in Durango to attend a friend's wedding and to join in the annual birthday hike for Helen's dad. However, once arriving in town, the remaining weekends in August quickly filled with plans to run, camp and visit with friends. We decided to stay in the Durango area for much of August and early September, adventuring around the San Juan mountains during the weeks between our weekend plans. Here are some of the many many highlights from our time in Durango.
  • The day after we arrived in Durango, I went on a big run with Caeley, Helen's brother's girlfriend. We started at Vallecito Lake, ran up Columbine Pass into the Chicago Basin, then traversed the Animas River to the Purgatory Ski Area. It was a 30ish mile day with lots of elevation gain and stunning views of the San Juan mountains. It was my longest run in quite a while, but I didn't feel too bad, and it motivated me to do some more exploring in the San Juans.
  • Our first weekend in town was spent on Mac's (father-in-law) birthday hike. A big group of 10 to 15 of us hiked a 13 mile loop in the mountains outside Pagosa Springs. It was a great outing with lots of fun conversation, a swim in a lake and some frisbee playing. Afterwards, everyone regrouped at Helen's parents for a fun party with tasty food.
  • The next weekend was Araaa (Helen's childhood friend) and Adri's wedding. It was a lovely ceremony followed by a night of fun dancing and delicious food. It was our first time meeting Adri, because he and Araaa live in Spain! It was great to spend some time with them and get to know them better in the weeks preceeding their wedding.
  • The next big item on the agenda was Caeley's 100 mile foot race, where I offered to pace her for a 25-mile stretch. Helen, Joe (brother-in-law) and I drove up along the Dolores River to meet Caeley at the trailhead around the 50 mile mark of the race. Shortly after we started running together, the sun went down and we spent the next six or so hours running in the dark before handing her off to her brother around 2am to pace the remainder of the race. The next morning, I looked up pictures of the trail we had run, and was bummed to see that if the sun were out, we would have had magnificent views in all directions. I'll have to go back in the daylight! We drove back to the finish line and all cheered as Caeley finished the race!
  • One of the weekends we camped with Helen's childhood friend Shannon, her husband Ty, and their two little kids, Rylan and Grayson. We love spending time with the kids, and we had a great weekend together. We went on a little hike, threw rocks in the river, played with toy tractors and excavators (which I often mixed up, only to get corrected by Grayson), and ate far too many s'mores.
  • After our camping trip, I drove down to Albuquerque to visit my friends Aidan and Rosie (although Rosie was sadly out of town 😿). During my visit, Aidan and I spent lots of time biking and running on the trails near his house. Each night we watched a movie and made a tasty dinner, including a homemade pizza, like we used to do when we lived together during college. I had been meaning to visit for a while, so it was great to finally make it down there and spend time with an old friend.
  • To celebrate our one year wedding anniversary, Helen and I went on a five day trip around southwest Colorado. We started with a night camping in the La Plata mountains with Helen's brothers and mom. It ended up being a rainy day, so we posted up under a tarp and spent our time playing cards, eating zucchini bread and attempting to start a campfire. The next day, we drove up towards Telluride, where we camped for three nights. We went on a few very beautiful hikes in the area, explored the town of Telluride, and bought way-too-expensive hamburgers at a place in town. The campground we stayed at was tucked in the aspens, and we decided we would have to come back in a few months to see the fall colors. We looped back towards Durango through Ouray, where we spent the day soaking in some lovely hot springs, before finding a campsite near Silverton. The next day, we explored the cute town of Silverton, then went on a pleasant hike up Lime Creek. We ended the trip with a sushi dinner in Durango and a soak in Durango Hot Springs.


- Colin
